content.title: Facts, Rankings & Recognition | Gonzaga University
content.text: Facts, Rankings & Recognition What does it mean to be a Zag?While facts and figures only begin to tell the story, these stats offer a window into what our university's all about. What Inspires You? Top Ranked Student Outcomes Value, Aid & Scholarships Student Life Schools & Programs #48 Most Innovative Universities(US News & World Report, 2026) 12:1 Student-to-faculty ratio 95% Graduates employed, pursuing higher degrees or in service orgs (2021-2023) #17 Best Undergraduate Teaching (U.S. News & World Report, 2026) Quick Facts Gonzaga is a nationally ranked liberal arts university rooted in the Pacific Northwest, with academic experiences and connections that span the globe. Committed to the Jesuit tradition of developing the whole person, Gonzaga prepares students for lives of leadership and service for the common good – academically, professionally and beyond. Type: Private Liberal Arts Carnegie Classification: National University Religious Affiliation: Roman Catholic (Jesuit) Established: 1887 Location: Spokane, Washington Campus Setting: Situated along the Spokane River, one-half mile from downtown business district Pronunciation: Gone - ZAG (as in "bag") - uh Enrollment: 7,470 Fields of Study: 16 undergraduate degrees through 53 majors, 68 minors and 73 concentrations; 23 master’s programs; and five doctorate degrees. Student/Faculty Ratio: 12 to 1 More Gonzaga Facts A Top Ranked University Recognized as a Best National University; listed in the top 24% of the 434 schools which received designation (U.S. News & World Report, 2026) Approved to join Phi Beta Kappa, the nation's oldest and most prestigious honor society (Phi Beta Kappa) Ranked No. 17 in the country for best undergraduate teaching (U.S. News & World Report, 2026) Ranked No. 48 in the country for most innovative universities ( (U.S. News & World Report, 2026) Named one of "The Best 390 Colleges" (The Princeton Review, 2026) U.S. News & World Report Recognition Read Story More Recognition Recognized as a Top Ten school for veterans, their spouses and military families (2025–26 Military Friendly School) Higher Education Excellence in Diversity (HEED) Award for comprehensive efforts in promoting diversity, equity and inclusion across campus. (Insight Into Diversity, 2024) No. 21 in the country for “Students Who Study Most." (The Princeton Review's "Best 390 Colleges: 2026 Edition") Recognized as one of the top 100 green colleges. (The Princeton Review's "Guide to Green College: 2025") No. 14 in the country for "Best Health Services" (The Princeton Review's "Best 389 Colleges: 2026 Edition") Ranked one of the "56 prettiest college campuses in America" (Condé Nast Traveler 2025) Named to the Forbes' America's Top Colleges List (Forbes, 2025) No. 15 in the country for excellence in service learning (U.S. News & World Report, 2026) Student Outcomes 93% of first-year students return for a second year, making Gonzaga’s retention rate one of the best in the nation. 93% of graduates secure jobs, graduate school admission, military service, or post-graduate service (e.g., Peace Corps, Teach for America, Jesuit Volunteer Corps) within one year of graduation. 86% of undergraduates graduate within six years, compared to the national average of 65%.
